topic: What a seed map can and cannot show
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: What a seed map can and cannot show
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. At an imaginary botanical station, a seed collection was being prepared for an exhibition. Visitors would see labelled jars from thirty coastal sites. The exhibition designer wanted a map showing the distribution of each species. The botanist warned that a map of collected seeds was not automatically a map of where the plants existed.

B. Collectors had travelled along roads. Plants close to a safe stopping place were easier to sample, while inaccessible slopes received fewer visits. A blank area might therefore indicate a gap in sampling, rather than an absence of plants. Labels contained locations and dates but did not record how long collectors searched. Without that information, the team could not compare collecting effort reliably.

C. Storage created another uncertainty. Most packets had been dried before being placed in sealed containers, but a small group arrived in damp envelopes. Germination tests produced lower results for that group. Poor survival in storage was one possible explanation. Those seeds might also have been collected before they were mature. Because the handling history was incomplete, the team could not distinguish these causes.

D. The botanist recommended two map layers. One would mark confirmed collection sites; the other would show places not yet surveyed. She proposed a separate label for an unsuccessful germination test. Such a result should not be described as proof that the species had disappeared from its original habitat. Collection, storage and survival in the wild were different questions.

E. Remaining funds were spent on better records rather than additional jars. Future collectors would note search duration, habitat conditions and the route followed. Repeated visits would use the same protocol. This would improve comparisons even if the collection grew slowly. A large archive can look impressive, but its scientific value depends partly on whether users can identify what remains uncertain. The exhibition displayed a field notebook alongside the seeds to make that point visible.
